record.paper_title: The Statistical Model of Nuclear Reactions: Open Problems
record.original_question: In the statistical model of nuclear reactions, partial gamma decay widths for isolated neutron resonances are usually assumed to follow a Porter-Thomas distribution (PTD), and total gamma decay widths are then obtained by summing a very large number of such partial widths over many gamma decay channels. The paper asks whether replacing the PTD assumption for the partial gamma widths with a different distribution could produce a predicted distribution of total gamma decay widths for neutron resonances in the compound nucleus 96Mo that agrees better with the experimentally observed distribution, which is much broader and centered at larger values than the standard statistical-model prediction.

evidence.quote: That raises the question: Would a distribution of partial gamma widths different from the PTD yield better agreement of the predicted distribution of total gamma widths with the data of Ref. [3]?
However, Fig. 6 shows that use of the modified distribution for the gamma channels does not affect the disagreement with the data of Ref. [3].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a compound nucleus formed at neutron-resonance energies. In the standard statistical model, each isolated resonance λ has partial gamma decay widths Γ_{λc} into many gamma decay channels c = 1, …, N (with N very large), and the total gamma decay width is Γ_λ = Σ_{c=1}^N Γ_{λc}. Under the usual hypothesis the partial widths Γ_{λc} are independent random variables, each distributed according to a Porter–Thomas distribution (i.e. Γ_{λc}/⟨Γ_{λc}⟩ is distributed as a chi-squared variable with one degree of freedom). Summing N such independent partial widths yields, for large N, a predicted distribution P_PT(Γ) of total gamma widths that is sharply peaked about its mean.

For the compound nucleus ^{96}Mo, the experimentally observed distribution of total gamma decay widths over many neutron resonances is found to be much broader than P_PT(Γ) and to be centered at substantially larger values of Γ than the statistical-model mean.

Question: Does there exist an alternative probability distribution f(x) on [0, ∞) (with finite mean), used in place of the Porter–Thomas distribution for each normalized partial gamma width Γ_{λc}/⟨Γ_{λc}⟩, such that, when N independent partial widths drawn from f are summed to form the total width Γ_λ, the resulting predicted distribution of total gamma widths reproduces the empirically observed broader distribution, located at larger values of Γ, of total gamma decay widths of neutron resonances in ^{96}Mo? If so, exhibit such an f; if not, prove that no choice of f (subject to standard finiteness assumptions) can reconcile the statistical-model prediction with the observed distribution.
artifact.status_search_result: The internal analysis associated with this question indicates that replacing the Porter–Thomas distribution with a modified distribution for the partial gamma channels does not remove the discrepancy with the ^{96}Mo data, suggesting a negative answer within the framework considered. However, no fully general impossibility proof covering all alternative distributions appears to be established, and the broader puzzle of the ^{96}Mo total gamma-width distribution remains an active topic in nuclear-reaction statistics.

status_evidence.title: The Statistical Model of Nuclear Reactions: Open Problems (arXiv:1810.13385)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion notes that use of a modified distribution for the gamma channels does not affect the disagreement with the ^{96}Mo data.
status_evidence.claim: Within the considered modification, replacing PTD by an alternative distribution for partial gamma widths fails to reproduce the observed broader, shifted distribution of total gamma widths in ^{96}Mo.
